'''Darrell Antwonne Arthur''' (born March 25, 1988) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player.  He played college basketball for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] for two seasons, and was part of their [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2007–08 national championship team]]. He was drafted by the [[New Orleans Hornets]] in the [[2008 NBA draft]] but after two trades, he ended up with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], with whom he signed on July 8, 2008.<ref>{{cite news|publisher=NBA |url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_sign_first_round_draft_picks-080708.html |title=Grizzlies Sign Arthur |date=July 8, 2008 |access-date=July 19, 2008 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080720023906/http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_sign_first_round_draft_picks-080708.html |archive-date=July 20, 2008 }}</ref> He is listed at {{convert|6|ft|9|in}}, {{convert|235|lb|abbr=on}} and played the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position.

Darrell is now a part of the Denver Nuggets Front Office.

Arthur is the first cousin of fellow basketball player [[Quinton Ross]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=1765 |title=Grizzlies sign Quinton Ross |publisher=[[Inside Hoops]] |url-status=live |archive-date=June 29, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140629190045/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=1765 }}</ref>

==Early life==
In high school, Arthur guided [[South Oak Cliff High School]] to back-to-back Texas 4A state titles in 2005 and 2006 and was the tournament's MVP both years. Those state titles were later forfeited, after it was determined that the school had played an ineligible athlete.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.wfaa.com/news/local/64806217.html |title=South Oak Cliff High School stripped of another basketball title |work=[[WFAA]] |author=Brett Shipp |date=February 20, 2009 |access-date=February 22, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407073942/http://www.wfaa.com/news/local/64806217.html |archive-date=April 7, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

During his senior year, Arthur was named a [[McDonald's All-American]] and third-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] honors in 2006.

In regards to college recruiting, Arthur was considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], and [[247Sports.com]] listed him as the consensus top recruit in Texas and the 13th best recruit in the country.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Darrell-Arthur-22048 Darrell Arthur – Yahoo! Sports]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Darrell-Arthur-64976/high-school-113899/|title = Darrell Arthur, South Oak Cliff, Power Forward}}</ref>

==College career==
Arthur's uniform number in college was 00, making him the first Jayhawk to wear that number since [[Greg Ostertag]]. He was named to the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] All-Rookie team in his freshman year in 2006–07. Arthur was named to the All-Big 12 first team the year Kansas won the  [[List of NCAA Men's Division I Basketball champions|NCAA championship]].

==Professional career==

===Memphis Grizzlies (2008–2013)===
Arthur was selected by the [[New Orleans Hornets]] as the 27th overall pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]] but was promptly traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for cash. The Trail Blazers then traded Arthur to the [[Houston Rockets]] for draft rights to 25th overall pick [[Nicolas Batum]]. Soon afterwards, the Rockets traded Arthur to the Memphis Grizzlies for draft rights to the 28th overall pick [[Donté Greene]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/writers/luke_winn/06/27/winn.arthur/index.html |title=Arthur Traded 3 times on draft night, ends up with Grizzlies |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=June 27, 2008 |access-date=July 19, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080723165038/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/writers/luke_winn/06/27/winn.arthur/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 23, 2008 }}</ref>

On September 3, 2008, Arthur and fellow former Kansas Jayhawks teammate [[Mario Chalmers]] were excused from NBA's Rookie Training Camp following a marijuana-related incident.<ref>{{cite news|author=Chris Broussard |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3567481 |title=Chalmers, Arthur caught with marijuana at rookie camp |publisher=[[ESPN.com]] |work=[[ESPN The Magazine]] |date=September 4, 2008 |access-date=September 4, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024125843/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/news/story?id=3567481 |url-status=live |archive-date=October 24, 2012 }}</ref> Police responding to their hotel room following a fire alarm at 2:00 a.m. claimed that the room smelled strongly of marijuana but none was found and no charges were filed. Fellow NBA rookie [[Michael Beasley]] was also reported to have been in the room at the time, but was not asked to leave camp.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.faniq.com/blog/Michael-Beasley-Was-In-The-Room-With-Darrell-Arthur-And-Mario-Chalmers-When-They-Were-Busted-For-Marijuana-Blog-11621 |title=Perhaps The Concerns About Michael Beasley Were Warranted |date=September 5, 2008 |access-date=September 5, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006082305/http://www.faniq.com/blog/Michael-Beasley-Was-In-The-Room-With-Darrell-Arthur-And-Mario-Chalmers-When-They-Were-Busted-For-Marijuana-Blog-11621 |archive-date=October 6, 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|work=[[WIBW-TV]] |date=September 3, 2008 |url=http://www.wibw.com/home/headlines/27823029.html |title=Report: Arthur, Chalmers Sent Home from Rookie Camp |access-date=September 11, 2008 |url-status=live |archive-date=February 15, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120215050758/http://www.wibw.com/home/headlines/27823029.html }}</ref> Beasley was fined $50,000 for his involvement in the incident.<ref>{{cite news|agency=[[Associated Press]] |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/news/story?id=3596442 |title=Beasley fined $50,000 for involvement in Rookie Transition Program incident |access-date=September 11, 2008 |date=September 18, 2008 |url-status=live |archive-date=October 24, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024173640/http://sports.espn.go.com/mlb/news/story?id=3596442 }}</ref>
Arthur released a statement denying any involvement with marijuana.<ref>{{cite news|author=Ronald Tillery |url=http://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2008/sep/05/arthur-says-he-learned-lesson/ |title=Arthur says he learned lesson |date=September 5, 2008 |url-status=live |archive-date=February 12, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120212222922/http://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2008/sep/05/arthur-says-he-learned-lesson/ }}</ref> Arthur was fined $20,000 by the league for missing the rookie camp, but was not fined or suspended for any drug-related violations.<ref>{{cite news|date=September 10, 2008 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3579879 |title=Chalmers, Arthur fined $20,000 after rookie symposium incident |agency=Associated Press |work=ESPN.com |url-status=live |archive-date=October 24, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024143840/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/news/story?id=3579879 }}</ref>

On June 29, 2012, the Grizzlies extended a qualifying offer to Arthur, making him a restricted free agent.<ref>{{cite web|title=Grizzlies extend qualifying offers to Arthur and Speights |work=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-extend-qualifying-offers-arthur-and-speights |date=June 29, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120702115335/http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-extend-qualifying-offers-arthur-and-speights |url-status=live |archive-date=July 2, 2012 |access-date=June 29, 2012 }}</ref>

===Denver Nuggets (2013–2018)===
On June 27, 2013, Arthur was traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] along with 55th overall draft pick [[Joffrey Lauvergne]] in exchange for [[Kosta Koufos]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Nuggets Acquire F Darrell Arthur From Memphis Grizzlies |url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-f-darrell-arthur-memphis-grizzlies |work=NBA.com |date=June 27, 2013 |access-date=June 28, 2013 |archive-date=July 1, 2013 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130701013940/http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-f-darrell-arthur-memphis-grizzlies }}</ref> On June 23, 2014, he exercised his player option for the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/06/23/nuggets-moves.ap/index.html |title=Nuggets' Arthur, Robinson exercise player options |date=June 23, 2014 |access-date=August 26, 2014 |archive-date=June 24, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140624054512/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/06/23/nuggets-moves.ap/index.html }}</ref>

On August 7, 2015, Arthur re-signed with the Nuggets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-re-sign-darrell-arthur-will-barton-and-jameer-nelson|title=Nuggets Re-Sign Darrell Arthur, Will Barton and Jameer Nelson|work=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2015|access-date=August 7, 2015}}</ref> On March 31, 2016, he tied a career high with 24 points off the bench in a 101–95 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160331/DENNOP/gameinfo.html|title=Babbitt leads Pelicans past Nuggets 101-95|date=March 31, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 1, 2016}}</ref>

On July 9, 2016, Arthur again re-signed with the Nuggets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-re-sign-forward-darrell-arthur-070916|title=Denver Nuggets Re-Sign Forward Darrell Arthur|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2016|access-date=July 9, 2016}}</ref>

On July 13, 2018, Arthur was traded, along with [[Kenneth Faried]], a protected 2019 first round draft pick and a 2020 second round draft pick, to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Isaiah Whitehead]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/07/13/brooklyn-nets-acquire-kenneth-faried-darrell-arthur-denver-nuggets|title=Brooklyn Nets acquire Kenneth Faried, Darrell Arthur from Denver Nugget|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2018|access-date=July 13, 2018}}</ref> Seven days later, Arthur was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for [[Jared Dudley]] and a 2021 second round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2018/07/20/brooklyn-nets-complete-trade-phoenix-suns|title=Brooklyn Nets Complete Trade With Phoenix Suns|work=NBA.com|date=July 20, 2018|access-date=July 20, 2018}}</ref> On October 15, 2018, he was waived by the Suns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-waive-arthur-harrison|title=Suns Waive Arthur, Harrison|work=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2018|access-date=October 15, 2018}}</ref>
